UPSTREAM: ath10k: reject 11b tx fragmentation configuration Even though there's a WMI enum for fragmentation threshold no known firmware actually implements it. Moreover it is not possible to rely frame fragmentation to mac80211 because firmware clears the "more fragments" bit in frame control making it impossible for remote devices to reassemble frames. Hence implement a dummy callback just to say fragmentation isn't supported. This effectively prevents mac80211 from doing frame fragmentation in software. This fixes Tx becoming broken after setting fragmentation threshold. Fixes: 1010ba4c5d1c ("ath10k: unregister and remove frag_threshold callback") Signed-off-by: Michal Kazior <michal.kazior@tieto.com> Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@qca.qualcomm.com> (cherry picked from commit 92092fe528e79c9bd25784ca0ef341d5a1d1b642) TEST=none BUG=none Change-Id: Iaa697a13526c1a8d987b47e399b7a966665e99ce Signed-off-by: Anilkumar Kolli <akolli@codeaurora.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/307341 Commit-Ready: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Tested-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: ath10k: don't remove peer that doesn't exist If peer creation failed during offchannel Tx the driver attempted to delete the peer nonetheless. This caused the ar->num_peers counter to be incorrectly decremented. This subsequently could cause the counter to drop below 0 and also eventually lead to firmware crash because host would think there are less peer entries created in firmware then there really were. Signed-off-by: Michal Kazior <michal.kazior@tieto.com> Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@qca.qualcomm.com> (cherry picked from commit adaeed74bc085bc59991cd6e23ee7f720b6c6aab) TEST=none BUG=none Change-Id: Ia1d83d7cc15d931c89e04b2d8a5d204a231ca8ef Signed-off-by: Anilkumar Kolli <akolli@codeaurora.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/307346 Commit-Ready: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Tested-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: usb: gadget: configfs: Let composite_setup handle setup requests android_setup() iterates over the list of available function drivers attempting to find one that will handle the setup request. This has several issues: 1) it's the list of available functions, not the ones actually used in the current configuration, 2) the corresponding function structures may not have been setup yet, or may have been freed already, and 3) access to the list must be protected by the gi->lock mutex. Since composite_setup() already does the right thing here by calling the setup() callback for functions that are actually part of the configuration (with the proper locking), kill off the loop over the available_func list. BUG=b:25356151 TEST=Switch configurations between MTP/PTP/ADB/MIDI on Smaug and plug/unplug USB cable. No crashes seen and everything still works as expected. Change-Id: I8d77d0d6a4c33ee0958e5d2ee3e7657f6b32d9b7 Fixes: bb2a9e71710e ("usb: gadget: Add Uevent to notify userspace") Signed-off-by: Andrew Bresticker <abrestic@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/309900 Reviewed-by: Badhri Jagan Sridharan <badhri@google.com> Reviewed-by: Vincent Palatin <vpalatin@chromium.org>

It also changes the polarity of the 'cold bootsrap' pin, so using the latest spiflash utility is mandatory. Note that there has been no signer changes. CHROMIUM: soc/tegra: pmc: Restore PMC_SCRATCH250 on resume It appears that PMC_SCRATCH250 gets cleared during LP0, so any reset occurring after an LP0 cycle will not execute the BootROM I2C commands programmed into the PMC scratch registers. Fix this by restoring PMC_SCRATCH250 in tegra_pmc_resume(). BUG=b:25111885,chrome-os-partner:45973 TEST=Trigger kernel panic after suspend/resume and observe that the bootreason is correctly reported as "kernel_panic".
